review.summary: Phase 20 chunk "qualification-and-package" delivers its declared scope with genuine, cross-bound evidence. I reconstructed commands_for(20) independently (commands_for(17)+commands_for(19), deduped and renamed) and it is exactly the 59 commands recorded in docs/checks/phase-20.json and the bound review copy, all at exit_code 0 with source_unchanged true against the reviewed hash ee60edd5; review_phase.check_evidence enforces ordered command equality, so no subset could satisfy the gate. Version is bumped to 0.2.2, and both clean package proofs are real 12-command executions on 1.89.0/1.99.0 with requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, and three external-crate consumers each (including the new response_compatibility consumer). scripts/check-access-release.py re-verifies the retained archives byte-for-byte, asserts identical files/vcs across compilers, requires releaseCommit == HEAD, and compares every packaged file against both the working tree and the release commit blobs — so "current packaged bytes verified against the committed clean source" is mechanically established rather than asserted. The differing per-compiler archive digests are explained correctly in docs/PACKAGING.md:94-96 as container metadata. The 49-job matrix is wired (24 features x 2 toolchains + 1) with both json-unification and red-team-json-unification retained, pinned by tools/test_ci.py:111 and the documented-count assertions; docs/CI.md:158-163 honestly states the CI subset is 41 commands and excludes package execution, and I confirmed 59 minus 18 native/fixture commands equals 41. Live qualification was actually re-run at 0.2.2 (attempt 14, 2026-10-19T06:04Z) and tools/live_evidence.py:266 forces the receipt's runtimeInputsSha256 to equal the current runtime fingerprint, with 403/400 outcomes and not_needed cleanup reported without inflation. Ledgers are regenerated and --check-verified from hashed audit/cases/outcomes inputs, the 76 retained UUID checks and query-option behavior are documented, and the release documentation tests are generalized (version-vs-publication conditional plus a synthetic 0.2.2 receipt test) so no self-referential archive hash is embedded in packaged files. CHANGELOG.md makes no publication or consumer-adoption claim absent receipts. Remaining items are narrow and all low: docs/SECURITY.md is in declared chunk scope yet its Runtime boundaries section is silent on the response string-format relaxation; no document states that the delivery push must not carry [skip ci] even though every recent commit does and tools/release_delivery.py requires a terminal run whose commit equals remote main; the live receipt path regex hardcodes phase-08; the contracts-and-package CI job never packages; and the --require-clean package step sits outside the gated command list. None of these undermine the chunk's deliverables.

findings.description: docs/SECURITY.md is declared chunk scope_evidence, but its "Runtime boundaries" section still describes only request-side validation ("Destinations, path segments, headers, request bodies and typed schemas validate before authentication") and never discloses that response modes no longer assert the uuid, rfc3339, datetime, date, duration, email, url and regex string formats across the 172 frozen roots with format checks. The disclosure exists in CHANGELOG.md:13-15 and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:124-130, and line 32 already disclaims trust in returned URLs, so this is an omission rather than an inaccuracy — but a reader consulting the security model document alone would not learn that this defense-in-depth layer was intentionally narrowed.
findings.required_fix: Add one bullet to the Runtime boundaries list stating that response validation deliberately ignores the eight named string-format assertions while retaining string types, baseline presence/type/bounds, finite JSON and resource limits, and link docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md for the full loosened/retained rule set.

findings.description: The procedure requires "actual terminal success for all 49 configured CI jobs before phase completion", and tools/release_delivery.py:94-96 additionally requires refs/heads/main to equal the CI run's commit with a matching source fingerprint. Every recent commit (d64d9dc, 938adbe, e4cabb0, 2908a98, 16e4cf7) carries [skip ci], and no document in the repository mentions [skip ci] at all. The delivery push can therefore satisfy the documented steps yet produce no workflow run for the final main commit, blocking the next chunk's required receipt.
findings.required_fix: State explicitly in docs/RELEASE.md (and mirror in docs/CI.md's delivery section) that the commit pushed to main for delivery must not contain a [skip ci] marker, since the terminal 49-job receipt must belong to that exact commit.

findings.description: The controlled live receipt path is constrained to the literal pattern docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-\d{2}\.json, so the 0.2.2 run executed for phase 20 is filed as docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-14.json and referenced that way from contracts/live-evidence.json:4, docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:13 and docs/phase-status.json:4339. The receipt content is correctly bound to the current runtime fingerprint and crate version, so the evidence is sound, but the phase-08 filename is now a misnomer that makes the live evidence trail harder to follow across the 0.2.x track.
findings.required_fix: Either widen the pattern to accept a phase-scoped prefix (for example phase-\d{2}-live-attempt-NN) while keeping the historical names valid, or add an explicit note in docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md that the phase-08-live-attempt-* filenames are a retained historical naming convention rather than a phase attribution.

findings.description: The job named contracts-and-package runs tools/check_phase.py --phase 20 --verification-only --contracts-only, and ci_commands_for in tools/check_phase.py:512-515 explicitly filters out scripts/check-package.py and scripts/check-access-release.py, so this job never packages anything. The misleading name is also baked into the required CI context set computed by tools/release_delivery.py:66, meaning the delivery receipts will permanently record a package-sounding context that performs no package check. docs/CI.md:158-160 does disclose the exclusion, which limits the impact to naming.
findings.required_fix: Rename the job to reflect its actual scope (for example contracts-gate) and update the matching context derivation in tools/release_delivery.py:66, tools/test_ci.py and docs/CI.md; alternatively add an inline workflow comment stating that package and candidate-guard execution is local-only.

findings.description: scripts/check-package.py --require-clean is a manual documented step and is deliberately absent from commands_for(20), so the clean-repository precondition itself is not reproducible from the phase gate; scripts/check-access-release.py:81 and scripts/verify-publication.py:40 consume the recorded requireClean/effectiveDirty fields from the proof JSON. This is consistent with the trust model in docs/PHASES.md:7 (repository writers are trusted) and is strongly mitigated because the gate independently re-derives the archive digest, file inventory, VCS identity and every packaged byte against HEAD, but the cleanliness attestation remains self-reported.
findings.required_fix: Note in docs/RELEASE.md and docs/PACKAGING.md that requireClean/effectiveDirty are self-reported attestations covered by the repository-writer trust model, and that the independently re-derived evidence is the archive digest, file inventory, VCS identity and byte comparison against the release commit.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-20.json:2-6 and docs/reviews/phase-20-chunk-qualification-and-package-attempt-02.checks.json are the same run (checked_at 2026-10-19T08:11:38.178159+00:00, source_sha256 ee60edd531d651fb2583723f101eddd65d297a8c1dad030828092dbe4f267faa, passed true); both contain exactly 59 invocation records and every exit_code is 0, with no timeout true and no unexecuted entry.

I reconstructed commands_for(20) from tools/check_phase.py:71-87 as commands_for(17)+commands_for(19) deduped: 38 phase-17 commands (including commands_for(12)[4:25] = 21 contract/generation commands) plus 18 new phase-19 commands plus generate_models --verify-fixtures plus two check-native-exports = 59, matching the recorded set exactly. tools/review_phase.py:187 enforces [item['command'] for item in checks] == commands_for(phase), so a partial run cannot pass the gate.

crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:3 is version = "0.2.2"; the packaged example is registered at line 76. docs/checks/phase-20-release-package-1.89.0.json:4-20 and -1.99.0.json:4-19 both record passed true, requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, dirtyFieldPresent false, releaseCommit d64d9dc7f71d95eaa1e7849e661c252660970914, with 12 cargo checks each at exit_code 0.

scripts/verify-publication.py:31-53 (require_proof) rejects any proof lacking schemaVersion 2, passed true, requireClean true, effectiveDirty false, a 40-hex releaseCommit, a matching rustcVersion prefix, all-zero exit codes, and the six required command prefixes including three 'run --locked' external consumer executions. Both phase-20 proofs satisfy this and record publicConsumerSourceSha256, accessPolicyConsumerSourceSha256 and responseCompatibilityConsumerSourceSha256.

scripts/check-access-release.py:68-108 requires proof releaseCommit == git HEAD, re-reads the retained .local/artifacts archive and recomputes its sha256/bytes, re-inspects the archive inventory and VCS, compares the archive src/examples set against the live filesystem, and byte-compares every packaged file against both the working tree and git show <releaseCommit>:<path>. Line 114 asserts the two compiler proofs share identical releaseCommit, files and vcs, which explains and bounds the differing archive digests 51ea02c8... (1.89.0) and 1e5085b7... (1.99.0).

scripts/check-package.py:27-60 refuses tar.extractall, rejects absolute/traversal/control-character/duplicate members, enforces the root-file and src/examples include policy, rejects development or credential inputs, bounds per-file (16 MiB), total (64 MiB) and count (2048), and requires .cargo_vcs_info.json plus self-contained source. Lines 189-191 execute the packaged examples/response_compatibility.rs from a separate consumer crate against the extracted archive.

crates/scm-sdk/examples/response_compatibility.rs exercises the reported defect cases offline through the public API only: opaque job-1/p-1/map-1 ids, both reported timestamp forms ("2026-01-05 00:00:00" and "2026-01-05T00:00:00.123456"), novel enum values, unknown nested fields, exact round-trip equality (lines 57-58, 118-119), u64::MAX projection fallback with is_unset assertions (lines 131-136), the three deliberately retained structural rejections (lines 60-79), and Mode::Request still erroring (lines 80, 121).

crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1221-1229 gates the bypass on mode.is_response() for exactly the eight named format kinds plus min/max carrying requestOnly true; lines 1199-1218 still parse and validate the check metadata before any skip, and line 1241 makes unknown check kinds fail closed.

tools/live_evidence.py:255-276 constrains the receipt path, verifies the receipt digest against contracts/live-evidence.json, and requires envelope sourceUnchanged true, exitCode 0, toolchain 1.99.0, a sanitized commandTemplate, and envelope runtimeInputsSha256 == runtime_fingerprint(root); validate_report lines 138-150 require crateVersion == the current Cargo.toml version. docs/checks/phase-08-live-attempt-14.json:4-33 records executedAt 2026-10-19T06:04:12Z, crateVersion 0.2.2 and cleanupState not_needed.

.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90 lists 24 feature selections including json-unification, red-team-json-unification and gateway-json-unification across toolchains 1.89.0/1.99.0; tools/test_ci.py:111 asserts toolchains x features + 1 == 49 and lines 113-125 bind the documented job counts in docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md. docs/CI.md:158-163 states the CI subset is 41 commands and excludes Rust, package, native-export probe, candidate-guard and verify-fixtures execution, which matches 59 minus the 18 native/fixture commands.

tools/g25_report.py:81-88 binds the generated ledger to auditSha256, casesSha256 and outcomesSha256 and lines 258-260 reject a corpus digest mismatch; the gate ran g25_audit.py --check, g25_fixtures.py --check and g25_report.py --check at exit 0, so docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md and contracts/compatibility/g25/comparison.json are current with their sources. The 76 UUID call sites in CHANGELOG.md:52 and docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:135 match requestUuidOccurrences 76 in contracts/compatibility/g25/audit.json:44187.

docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:52 discloses 213 residual-strictness corpus cases across 6 operations where a vendor-valid mutated document is rejected because frozen TypeScript also rejects it, and line 60 discloses that the relaxation reaches 172 frozen roots including management, IAM, Model Security and Gateway. Both are consequences the accepted plan (docs/g25-response-compatibility-plan.md:43-57) explicitly chose and required to be disclosed.

tools/test_ci.py:328-332 generalizes the release documentation assertion: receipt-specific checks apply only when the workspace version equals the recorded publication version, and tools/test_ci.py:353-359 exercises the 0.2.2 linked-receipt path on a synthetic fixture, so no self-referential archive hash is required inside packaged files. tools/test_release_022.py:26-56 pins the (20, '0.2.2') release pair, rejects unreviewed pairs, and proves each of the four archive examples and all three consumer executions are individually required.

tools/review_phase.py:68-83 implements the maintainer rubric exactly: blocker/high rejects outright, chunks need total >= 42 with every category >= 8, phases need >= 46, and the fifth-attempt exception requires total strictly > 40 plus recorded findings or limitations; lines 86-105 verify every prior attempt's prompt, CLI envelope and structured output, so an exception cannot be reached by jumping to attempt five. Lines 429-431 require supplied chunk scope to equal the declared scope_evidence.

tools/review_phase.py:15-16 excludes only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the source fingerprint, and the entire dirty/untracked set in the working tree falls inside those exclusions, so source_unchanged true is consistent with the reported git status.

The full tools suite run recorded 335 tests OK with a single justified skip ('This dependency freeze applies to the historical 0.1.1 patch'); scripts/check-native-exports.py passed on both compilers with frozenCapabilities 3820, and generate_models.py --verify-fixtures reported 27479 typed cases with 0 failures.

docs/phase-status.json:4387-4454 records explicit dispositions for all six attempt-01 findings, an evidence correction noting the reviewer's 56-command prose versus the actual 59 recorded commands, and candidate_private_scan passed at head d64d9dc with final bookkeeping scan openly marked pending.
limitations: Read-only review: I executed no commands, ran no builds or tests, and made no network calls. Compiler, package, live and CI outcomes are assessed from recorded artifacts, which I checked for exit codes, command identity against commands_for(20), internal cross-binding and source-hash consistency rather than re-running them.

The retained archives under .local/artifacts (for example scm-sdk-0.2.2-51ea02c84ba75f63.crate) were not opened by me; their digests and inventories are attested by the recorded proofs and by scripts/check-access-release.py's recorded re-verification at exit 0.

Per instruction I did not read credential or tenant-registration files, and nothing outside this repository. The live receipt was assessed only through its sanitized envelope and the guard that binds it to the current runtime fingerprint; I cannot independently confirm service-side behavior.
The reported 17 airs-cli-rs loopback failures on the worf checkout remain unexecuted and unverifiable here, as the plan and CHANGELOG both state; no consumer adoption is claimed or verified.

Registry, tag and terminal 49-job CI receipts do not exist yet and belong to the separate declared registry-and-remote-delivery chunk. tools/release_delivery.py cannot currently run to completion, so I reviewed it only as a guard design and did not treat its absent receipts as a deficiency of this chunk.

Generated model and validation correctness (phase 19 scope) was spot-checked at validation.rs:1199-1246 and through the independent fixture/oracle check results rather than re-audited; docs/checks files are excluded from the source fingerprint by design, so the declared package-proof scope evidence is bound through the hashed checks report and check-access-release rather than the source hash.
